segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Records, a merger, and Gulf risk
bullets: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi sites

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Wednesday, October seventh.
Today: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Arabia, oil stays above one hundred dollars, and Wall Street closes at records.
Plus a giant media merger is done, Google signs a big nuclear deal, and Southern California keeps baking. Let's go.

segments.strap: HOUTHIS CLAIM STRIKES ON SAUDI AIRPORT; RIYADH INTERCEPT
segments.headline: Houthis and Saudi Arabia

graphic.title: Yemen and Saudi Arabia
bullets: Houthis claim King Khalid Airport strikes
Saudi: ballistic missile intercepted north of Riyadh

lines.text: The A.P. reports the Houthis claim missile and drone strikes on King Khalid Airport in Riyadh and on military sites.
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted one ballistic missile north of the capital. Flight tracking showed a brief disruption. The strike claims are the Houthis' own. We have not confirmed them.
Both strands matter for oil, which is next.

segments.strap: BRENT $101.51, WTI $90.25 AS GULF RISK WEIGHS
segments.headline: Oil on Wednesday

graphic.title: Oil, early Wednesday
bullets: Gulf storm risk and Houthi attacks in view

lines.text: Reuters has Brent at one hundred one dollars and fifty-one cents early today. U.S. crude is at ninety dollars and twenty-five cents.
Reuters says Gulf storm risk and Houthi attacks are weighing against rising Middle East exports. It reports Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline moving five point eight million barrels a day.
That is Reuters' account. Brent has now been above one hundred dollars for several days running.

segments.strap: S&P 500 7,819 AND NASDAQ 27,600 BOTH CLOSE AT RECORDS
segments.headline: Wall Street at records

graphic.title: Tuesday's close
bullets: A.P.: S&P and Nasdaq both at records

lines.text: The A.P. reports the S and P five hundred rose six tenths of a percent to seven thousand eight hundred eighteen. The Nasdaq rose four tenths to twenty-seven thousand five hundred ninety-nine. Both are records.
The Dow gained five tenths. Small companies lagged: the Russell two thousand fell six tenths. Treasury yields eased.
The Federal Reserve's calendar lists minutes from its September meeting for today. None were posted when we checked.

One more number. Press reports say September payrolls rose just twenty-nine thousand, and unemployment is four point two percent. Traders see about a seventy-seven percent chance the Fed holds on October twenty-eighth. That is a market estimate, not a decision.

segments.strap: SKYDANCE COMPLETES WARNER BROS. DISCOVERY ACQUISITION
segments.headline: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery

graphic.title: The merger closes
bullets: Company release and SEC filing confirm close
Lamb Weston raises full-year profit outlook

lines.text: Skydance has completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The company's release and an S.E.C. filing say it closed on October sixth.
Elsewhere in business, the A.P. reports Anduril plans a three point seven billion dollar investment in a Baltimore-area shipyard to build nuclear-submarine components. That is a report of plans.
And Lamb Weston, the french fry maker, reported first-quarter sales of one point six seven billion dollars, up one percent. It raised its full-year profit outlook.

segments.strap: TRUMP SAYS IRAN COULD 'TAKE OUT' L.A. AND SAN DIEGO
segments.headline: Rally remark draws objections

graphic.title: Trump's Los Angeles remark
bullets: White House: he was explaining how he prevents the threat
No rally video or transcript located

lines.text: The A.P. reports President Trump said at a rally that Iran could take out Los Angeles and San Diego.
The White House later said he was explaining how he was preventing that threat. California officials objected.
We did not find the rally video or a transcript. The wording here rests on A.P. reporting.

segments.strap: REPUBLICAN GROUPS HAVE ABOUT $1B FOR MIDTERMS
segments.headline: Midterm money

stats.label: MAGA Inc. cash, end of Aug

lines.text: The A.P. reports Republican groups have about one billion dollars available for the midterms.
It says MAGA Inc. reported four hundred sixteen million dollars in cash at the end of August. A Senate-aligned Texas committee spent more than eighty-three million last month.
The elections are November third.

segments.headline: Nuclear power and a new model

graphic.title: Power and models
bullets: API: $0.68 in, $2.09 out per million tokens

lines.text: Google and Constellation announced a twenty-year agreement enabling eight hundred ninety megawatts of new nuclear capacity across eleven plants. There is also a fifteen-year supply deal for twenty-seven hundred megawatts.
Constellation says its investment will top four point three billion dollars. The power serves the Mid-Atlantic grid known as P.J.M.
In A.I., the French lab Mistral released Large 4 in public preview. It describes a one-trillion-parameter model, with forty-nine billion active at a time. Weights are expected by month's end.
Its listed price is sixty-eight cents per million input tokens and two dollars and nine cents for output.
Bitcoin showed about eighty-three thousand eight hundred dollars on Binance dot U.S., down two point seven percent in a day.
The Federal Register published two notices on October sixth. The Treasury's FinCEN withdrew its proposed crypto transaction requirements. It also withdrew a proposed special measure on crypto mixing.
And the Solana Foundation released an open-source tool for institutions to settle trades atomically. It says J.P. Morgan contributed settlement-practice input.

segments.strap: L.A. HITS 100°F FOUR OCTOBER DAYS IN A ROW; STORM ISAIAS
segments.headline: Heat out West, a Gulf storm

graphic.title: Weather
bullets: San Diego broke its 1987 daily record

lines.text: The Los Angeles Times reports four straight October days at or above one hundred degrees in Los Angeles. San Diego hit one hundred, breaking a ninety-seven-degree record set in nineteen eighty-seven.
In the Gulf, the Hurricane Center's five a.m. advisory has Tropical Storm Isaias with forty mile an hour winds, moving east-northeast. No coastal warnings are up, but strengthening is forecast.

segments.strap: PADRES 4, BREWERS 3; DODGERS 3, BRAVES 1 IN NLDS GAME 3
segments.headline: Baseball playoffs

graphic.title: NLDS Game 3
bullets: Padres' Mason Miller on paternity list

lines.text: In the playoffs, the Padres beat the Brewers four to three in Game 3. Milwaukee still leads that series two games to one. San Diego's closer Mason Miller went on the paternity list.
The Dodgers beat the Braves three to one in their Game 3. Today brings the A.L.D.S. Game 3s. Tigers and Mariners have split the first two, three to two each.

segments.strap: CREW-12 UNDOCKS TODAY; SPLASHDOWN THURSDAY; WEBB IMAGE
segments.headline: Space

graphic.title: Space
bullets: Schedule is subject to weather and readiness
Webb images NGC 7129 protostars and jets

lines.text: NASA says SpaceX Crew Twelve was scheduled to undock from the station today at eight oh five a.m. Eastern. Splashdown is planned for Thursday at eleven thirty-four a.m., subject to weather and readiness.
And NASA's Webb telescope released a new image of the nebula N.G.C. seventy-one twenty-nine, showing young stars and the jets they blast out.

segments.strap: EMMYS MOVE TO PRIME VIDEO IN 2027; STAYS FREE TO WATCH
segments.headline: Emmys find a new home

graphic.title: The Emmys on Prime Video
bullets: Ceremony stays free without a Prime subscription

lines.text: The Emmys are moving to Amazon Prime Video in twenty twenty-seven, under a six-year deal, the A.P. reports.
The ceremony is to remain free to watch without a Prime subscription.
